title: Honey Can Last for Thousands of Years
description: Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that had not rotted. Here is why honey lasts.

scenes.text: Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old, and it had not rotted.
scenes.subject: honey
scenes.say: [curious] Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old, and... [gasps] it had not rotted.

scenes.text: Honey is mostly sugar with very little water. Bacteria trying to live in it get the water pulled right out of them.
scenes.subject: honey
scenes.say: Honey is mostly sugar with very little water. [chuckles] Bacteria trying to live in it get the water pulled right out of them.

scenes.text: It is also slightly acidic, and bees add an enzyme that helps produce a little hydrogen peroxide, which fights germs.
scenes.subject: honey
scenes.say: It is also slightly acidic, and bees add an enzyme that helps produce a little hydrogen peroxide, which fights germs.

scenes.text: The trick is keeping it sealed. If honey soaks up moisture from the air, it can start to spoil.
scenes.subject: honey
scenes.say: [sighs] The trick is keeping it sealed. If honey soaks up moisture from the air, it can start to spoil.

scenes.text: Thank the bees for one of the longest lasting foods on Earth. Follow for more weird facts.
scenes.subject: bee
scenes.say: [warmly] Thank the bees for one of the longest lasting foods on Earth. [chuckles] Follow for more weird facts.
